theorem_contract.encoded_raw_merger: For branch inclusions J_e and any orthogonal branchwise Schur encoding B=direct_sum_e B_e, the raw merger is S_B=S B^*.
theorem_contract.frame_identity: S_B S_B^*=sum_e E_e=A and S_B^*S_B=B(S^*S)B^*; all nonzero singular values and conditioning are unchanged.
theorem_contract.polar_equivalence: polar(S_B)=A^(+/2)S B^*=polar(S)B^*, exactly the physical orientation-polar coisometry in Schur coordinates.
theorem_contract.conditional_compiler_reduction: If coherent B and B^* interfaces between the physical invariant ranges and Schur branches are compiled, physical and encoded polar compilers reduce to one another by one use of that interface.
theorem_contract.orientation_kernel_equivalence: For every isometric Schur flag embedding C, the joint-character factor obeys Gram(L C^*)=C(I tensor H_nu)C^* and polar(L C^*)=polar(L)C^*.
theorem_contract.physical_schur_interface: On Inv(V_nu^* tensor sigma_e), the source Schur decomposition has the exact form |Omega_nu> tensor B_e|m>. Unpreparing the canonical Bell invariant yields the opaque companion multiplicity state without exposing its basis.
theorem_contract.deterministic_environment_constraint: A branch-faithful isometry J_e x tensor eta_e requires <eta_e,eta_f>J_e^*J_f=0, so overlapping branches retain orthogonal which-path tags.
theorem_contract.raw_contraction_boundary: The largest scalar c making cS_B a contraction is 1/sqrt(||A||); the norm-one replacement is the unresolved polar.
theorem_contract.scope: This rejects Schur encoding as a free merger. It does not lower-bound a structured direct polar, a multi-round companion transform, or a decoder that retains orientation characters.

proof_obligations.resolution: The encoded raw merger and its polar are exact right-isometric transports of S and polar(S).
Every isometric flag embedding conjugates I tensor H_nu and leaves the analysis polar unchanged up to that embedding.
Overlapping physical ranges force orthogonal environment tags; deterministic transfer retains which-path information.
The equivalence identifies the exact target but supplies no circuit for A^(-1/2) or H_nu^(-1/2).

Schur orthogonality forces the invariant range to |Omega_nu> tensor multiplicity after the source decomposition; canonical Bell unpreparation gives the interface using the predecessor's uniform Schur circuit.
A decoder may avoid erasure by retaining characters; no all-n information extraction or classical separation is known.

adversarial_audit.objection: The larger Schur companion workspace makes cross-branch erasure unitary.
adversarial_audit.resolution: A branchwise isometry only conjugates the merger Gram and polar; orthogonal workspace does not create the missing overlaps.

adversarial_audit.objection: Using the Schur carrier requires first exposing a standard Kronecker multiplicity basis.
adversarial_audit.resolution: No. On the invariant support, the target/source irrep pair is the known Bell invariant and unprepares independently of the opaque companion multiplicity state.

adversarial_audit.objection: A deterministic Stinespring dilation can erase the branch into an unobserved environment.
adversarial_audit.resolution: For every nonzero cross-range overlap, isometry forces the corresponding environment tags to be orthogonal, so tracing them destroys the desired coherence.

adversarial_audit.objection: Scaling the raw merger to a contraction avoids inverse square roots.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It produces a lossy raw analysis map. Its normalized partial-isometric replacement is exactly A^(+/2)S_B.

adversarial_audit.objection: Polar equivalence proves the Schur companion route is computationally hard.
adversarial_audit.resolution: No circuit lower bound follows. The companion may expose structure useful for directly compiling the same polar.

adversarial_audit.objection: Every viable decoder must merge branches.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False. The retained-character route keeps the full Walsh register and remains a separate open architecture.

summary: Closed the free-Schur-merger loophole: orthogonal fixed-source Schur encodings preserve the full physical and joint-character Gram spectra, and their normalized mergers are exactly the existing orientation polars in encoded coordinates. A useful Schur route must therefore compile that polar using companion structure or avoid branch erasure.
falsifiers_triggered: Polynomial Schur isotypic routing does not itself produce cross-orientation coherence.
Deterministic branch-faithful transfer preserves purity only by retaining which-path tags on overlapping ranges.
An isometric coordinate enlargement cannot remove A^(-1/2) or H_nu^(-1/2).
